question: What is the add/drop window for a graduate third-term course?

question: Does missing all remaining classes automatically count as formally withdrawing from a course?
gold_answer: No. Simply not attending class does not constitute withdrawal.

question: Is course withdrawal still allowed in the last week of a graduate term?
gold_answer: No. Withdrawals are not accepted during the last week of the term.

question: A student working a full-time co-op is always prohibited from taking any course at the same time, correct?
gold_answer: No. A student on a full-time co-op may be permitted to take one course outside work hours, subject to applicable college policies.

question: Is CPT authorization tied to the specific employer and work location?
gold_answer: Yes. CPT authorization is specific to the employer and location, as well as dates and whether the work is full-time or part-time.

question: If an experiential learning position is unpaid, an eligible F-1 student does not need CPT authorization, correct?
gold_answer: No. CPT authorization is required for eligible unpaid experiential learning opportunities as well.

question: What review time does OGS give for a completed CPT request?
gold_answer: Up to 15 business days after receiving the completed request.

question: Does completing more than 364 days of full-time CPT at the same degree level affect OPT eligibility?
gold_answer: Yes. Exceeding 364 days of full-time CPT at the same degree level causes the student to lose OPT eligibility at that degree level.

question: If my CPT employer changes, can I assume my existing CPT authorization automatically covers the new employer?
gold_answer: No. CPT authorization is employer-specific, so a different employer is not automatically covered by the existing authorization.

question: What should an F-1 graduate student have in place before starting a university co-op in the United States?
gold_answer: The student should satisfy the university's graduate co-op eligibility requirements and obtain the required CPT authorization before beginning the employment.

question: A graduate student has completed 16 semester hours and has a 3.000 GPA. If the student is in F-1 status, is that alone enough to begin off-campus co-op employment immediately?
gold_answer: No. Completing 16 semester hours and having a 3.000 GPA are not by themselves sufficient. The student must satisfy the other applicable graduate co-op requirements, and an F-1 student must obtain the required CPT authorization from OGS before beginning employment.
